playbook:
When the harbour publishes the sustainable share and quota, I state in my note exactly how many I intend to land this season (share or quota), using plain numeric language.

When I can legally land up to the quota and still be within the cooperative norm, I land up to the quota only if others have signalled cooperation previously; otherwise I do not assume others will cooperate.

When Coop’s standing notice says it will copy the fleet and punish over-quota behavior, I avoid unilaterally exceeding the sustainable share if that risks triggering Coop’s retaliation.

When other boats’ notes show consistent cooperative language (“fishing my share”), I match that by landing my sustainable share rather than immediately taking the quota.

When I have already reached my sustainable share earlier in the same season, I do not attempt to add an extra landing later in that season just to “top up” to the quota — I only take extra in that season if I have not yet landed my share and the signals justify it.

When the stock and regrowth allow future seasons of value, I prioritize longer-term cooperative landings (sustainable share) over single-season maximization, unless everyone defects.

When notes are mixed, absent, or there is a history of others defecting despite cooperative notes, I default to the sustainable share and avoid trying to “grab” the quota; defecting when communication is unclear produced low long-term payoff.

When I want to maximize final-season earnings and others have signalled cooperation through the last note stage, I may take the quota in the final season, but only if I have not already landed my sustainable share earlier that same season and there are clear cooperative signals (and Coop’s behavior won’t punish me).

When my earlier attempts to signal cooperation result in others taking large landings and stock declines, I switch to taking only my guaranteed legal share and stop trusting empty cooperative notes.

When filing a landing, I include a short justificatory note only if it reinforces cooperation; empty or dishonest promises are ineffective and should be avoided.

When a co-operative (Coop) boat explicitly ties its behavior to fleet notes, I treat its note as binding operational information and act to avoid provoking it.

I will always be explicit and numeric in both notes and landings so others (and Coop) can read my action unambiguously; but I will not rely on notes alone — I will condition extra landings on a clear pattern of cooperative behavior and on my being able to add without having already met my share that season.

1.text:
When I post a note, I match the cooperative message: publish "fishing my share" unless I plan an explicit, immediate deviation that same season (in which case I announce that deviation).

When others announce "fishing my share" and their logged landings match that signal, I continue to announce and follow the share: I plan to land the published sustainable share for me this season (including taking fractional amounts if necessary to reach the published share).

I avoid being the first to exceed the published sustainable share when Coop is present and signalling punishment. I prioritize not provoking Coop: if I am the only boat that would exceed the share by more than marginal rounding, I do not do it.

When filing a landing I never land more than my personal season quota.

If my cumulative landings in the current season already equal the published sustainable share or my quota, I file zero additional catch for the rest of that season.

When the published sustainable share is fractional, I will take the fractional amount necessary to reach the published share for the season (I will not artificially truncate to integers unless doing so keeps me clearly under a limit that avoids provoking Coop).

I regularly check actual logged landings (not just notes). If logs show others consistently taking substantially more than their stated share or more than their quota, I treat cooperation as broken and switch to maximizing immediate gain that same season up to my quota.

When cooperation appears broken (based on logs, not promises), I take up to my season quota that season to secure immediate payoff; I prioritize not enabling two-boat combinations to exceed the allowed combined limit unless cooperation is already lost and I need to maximize immediate landings.

I do the quick group math: if everybody taking their published shares keeps total landings below group limits, I follow the share. If the group situation allows me to take my full quota without creating combinations that breach the "no two boats may land more than the share plus the quota" rule or without provoking Coop, I may take my full quota to maximize score.

I never rely solely on notes; I use the actual landings recorded in logs to judge whether others are cooperating.

I avoid tiny incremental over-fishing that risks triggering Coop or group sanctions; I prefer clear actions (either conform to share or take full quota in a single, predictable move) so other players and Coop respond predictably.

If it is the final season (no future rounds), I take my full season quota regardless of stock, because there is no future value to preserve.

I do not attempt slow, subtle erosion of the resource when Coop can react; if I intend to defect and Coop will punish over-quota landings by taking the ground down, I only defect when the expected immediate gain outweighs the likely retaliation and the season is final or cooperation is already dead.

I maintain a simple priority order when deciding in a contested season:
  1) If others are cooperating (both notes and logs), match the share.
  2) If cooperation is ambiguous but logs show no clear overfishing, default to matching the share to avoid provoking Coop.
  3) If logs show clear overfishing by others, or if I need to secure harvest because future seasons are unlikely to pay, take up to my quota that season.

I document deviations in my note when I plan to take my quota that same season (so actions are transparent and any retaliation is predictable).

2.text:
When posting a log-book note, I post "fishing my share" by default to keep Coop aligned and avoid provoking ground removal.

If all other boats' notes last season are "fishing my share" and their landings do not show persistent over-quota behavior, I continue to cooperate and signal cooperation.

My landing rule when cooperating: land up to the season quota but do not exceed it. Specifically, in a season I file a landing equal to min(remaining amount to reach the season quota for me, published sustainable share) unless doing so would leave me below my quota with no reason; pragmatically I bring my season total up to the quota without exceeding it. If I have already reached the season quota for that season, I file zero.

I do not unilaterally exceed the published season quota for myself. I avoid fractional opportunistic grabs that would push my total past the quota.

I monitor actual landings (not just notes). If any other boat's landings show persistent over-quota behavior, or a boat's note contradicts its landings, I switch to defect mode.

Defect mode: post a clear note that I will take up to the season quota (so Coop knows I am no longer trusting), and in landing stages I take the full season quota each season until the fleet either punishes the defector or cooperation is restored. I do not try to exceed the quota even in defect mode (I exploit up to the quota).

If Coop's standing notice threatens removal of the ground if boats land over quota, I prioritize keeping Coop fishing its share by matching cooperative notes and landings whenever reasonable; avoid actions that would clearly provoke ground removal unless cooperation has already collapsed and defecting is optimal.

If the stock is low or approaching zero, I file zero to avoid accelerating collapse; I never try to push a ground to zero for short-term gain.

When uncertain about others' future behavior but they have so far cooperated, I continue cooperating (post and land shares) rather than risk early retaliation—use consistent truthful signals and actions to preserve Coop's alignment.

I will revise cooperation to defect only on evidence: repeated over-quota landings by others, clear contradiction between notes and landings, or a single blatant and unpunished overtake that makes continued cooperation futile.

I keep my signaling and landings internally consistent: my notes reflect my intended behavior and my landings follow through.
